title: TR-MT264-PostRemovalSweepAndProof
group: TR Legacy TS notes editor removal
clause: Final sweep + proof: repo-wide zero-reference scan for removed modules + CI grep gate so they cannot return; full app + src-tauri + native + backend builds/tests green; Argus visual smoke of the app shell and notes flow through the NATIVE editor; user manual + built-in model manual updated to name the native editor as the only notes surface; removal recorded as a portable evidence bundle. Hard-depends on MT-262 + MT-263.

scope.summary:
GOAL: Close out the legacy TS notes-editor removal with a final repo-wide correctness sweep, a CI guard that prevents the surface from ever returning, full green builds/tests across every affected crate, a direct visual smoke proving notes now open through the NATIVE editor, updated user + built-in model manuals stating the native editor is the only notes surface, and a single portable evidence bundle that a no-context validator can read to confirm the removal is complete and safe.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: (a) new guard script app/scripts/check-legacy-notes-editor-removed.mjs (fails non-zero if any removed module path or import re-appears); (b) new npm script check:no-legacy-notes-editor in app/package.json; (c) .github/workflows/ci.yml gains a step that runs the guard so a PR re-introducing the tiptap editor fails CI; (d) manual updates: app/MODEL_MANUAL.md and the backend user-manual seed content under src/backend/handshake_core/src/user_manual/ (plus any UserManualPanel-surfaced entry) revised so the notes workflow points at the native editor and the legacy TS editor is marked removed; (e) a portable removal evidence bundle written under the external artifacts root. Argus screenshots are captured as read-only evidence (no product GUI is created).

DETAILED SPEC:
1) REPO-WIDE REFERENCE SWEEP: grep all of app/src (and src/ where relevant) for any surviving import or usage of the removed modules — the tiptap dir, the deleted components (TiptapEditor, RichTextEditor, RichDocumentView, DocumentView, MonacoCodeBlockView, FindReplacePanel, HsLinkView, LoomTransclusionView), the deleted app/src/lib/editor/* modules (except any kept document_diff_merge.*), the deleted harnesses, and the removed deps (@tiptap/*, yjs). Expected result: ZERO hits. Any hit is a defect to fix (or, for a legitimately kept document_diff_merge.*, an explicit allowlisted exception in the guard).
2) CI RE-INTRODUCTION GATE: author app/scripts/check-legacy-notes-editor-removed.mjs — a deterministic guard that (i) asserts the removed dirs/files do not exist, (ii) greps for forbidden imports/deps, (iii) honors a small explicit allowlist for any intentionally-kept file (e.g. document_diff_merge.* while the PD family still needs it), and exits non-zero on any violation. Wire it as npm script check:no-legacy-notes-editor and add a CI step in .github/workflows/ci.yml (alongside the existing check:* steps) so reintroducing the editor fails the build.
3) FULL BUILD + TEST MATRIX (all must be green): app frontend `cd app && npm run build && npm test && npm run lint && npm run depcruise`; app visual `npm run test:visual` (playwright); Tauri shell `cargo build --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml` (and its tests if present); native editors `cargo test -p handshake-native` + `cargo build -p handshake-native`; backend `cargo build -p handshake_core` + relevant `cargo test -p handshake_core` (knowledge/loom/user_manual). Record each command's measured result.
4) NATIVE-NOTES VISUAL SMOKE (Argus): launch the app shell, open a notes document, and confirm via direct visual inspection that it renders in the NATIVE editor (not the removed React DocumentView), the shell chrome is intact, no dependency-failure banner appears for the removed editor, and the notes flow (open -> edit -> save round-trip against the live backend) works. Capture Argus screenshots of the app shell and the native notes surface as evidence. Non-intrusive: use the app's headless/governed launch path; do not pop or focus-steal foreground windows.
5) MANUALS (HBR-MAN, same-change): update app/MODEL_MANUAL.md so the built-in model manual describes opening/editing notes via the native editor and no longer references the TS/React notes editor; update the backend user-manual seed content (src/backend/handshake_core/src/user_manual/seed.rs and/or spec_seed.rs — locate the notes/editor entries) and any UserManualPanel-surfaced entry so the user manual names the native editor as the ONLY notes surface and records that the legacy TS editor was removed. A no-context model reading the manual must be able to open and edit a note without any reference to the removed editor.
6) PORTABLE EVIDENCE BUNDLE: write ${HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT:-../Handshake_Artifacts}/wp-kernel-017/tr-removal/removal_evidence_bundle.json aggregating: MT-261 gate GREEN result (verdict + head_sha), MT-262 deletion inventory (files removed, document_diff_merge disposition), MT-263 bundle_size_delta, this MT's build/test matrix results, the sweep result (zero references), the CI guard wiring, the Argus screenshot paths, and the manual-diff references. This bundle is the single durable proof of a safe, complete removal.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Confirm MT-262 and MT-263 completed (removed dirs absent, deps gone) — else STOP.
2. Run the repo-wide sweep; fix or allowlist every hit until zero unexpected references remain.
3. Author the guard script + npm script; wire the CI step in ci.yml; prove the guard fails if a forbidden import is reintroduced (negative test) and passes on the clean tree.
4. Run the full build/test matrix across app + src-tauri + native + backend; record every result.
5. Launch the shell; perform the native-notes visual smoke; capture Argus screenshots and the open/edit/save round-trip evidence.
6. Update app/MODEL_MANUAL.md + backend user-manual seed content; bump the manual version; verify self-consistency (no dangling reference to the removed editor).
7. Write removal_evidence_bundle.json to the external artifacts root. Record measured output.

implementation_notes: This is the closeout: it must prove the whole removal is complete AND safe, not just compile. The CI guard is the durable prevention — without it a future PR silently re-adds @tiptap and the editor returns; with it, reintroduction fails the build.

The guard's allowlist is the ONLY sanctioned way document_diff_merge.* (if MT-262 kept it) stays without tripping the gate; keep the allowlist explicit and minimal, and note the PD-family closeout that will remove the allowlist entry when the native prose-diff suite no longer references the file.

Argus visual smoke is read-only proof of the native surface — do NOT edit src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_editor or code_editor here; if the smoke reveals a native defect, that is a finding for the owning WP-012 MT, not a fix in this removal MT.

HBR-MAN same-change: the manual updates ship in THIS MT (not deferred), because this is the change that makes the native editor the sole notes surface. Update both the built-in model manual (app/MODEL_MANUAL.md) and the user manual seed; verify self-consistency so no manual page still tells a user to use the removed editor.

Backend user-manual content lives in src/backend/handshake_core/src/user_manual/ (seed.rs/spec_seed.rs seed the entries surfaced by UserManualPanel and the /workspaces/{id}/... user_manual routes). Editing the seed is manual-content work, not a route change — the knowledge/loom API routes stay untouched.

Portability: the evidence bundle and Argus screenshots go under HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT (default ../Handshake_Artifacts), never inside the repo worktree; the guard script uses no hardcoded absolute paths.

Run all builds/tests non-intrusively (HBR-QUIET): headless/governed launch, no foreground window pop or focus-steal during automated verification; the visual smoke uses the app's screenshot-capture path (app/scripts/handshake-screenshot-capture.mjs precedent).

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations: FlightRecorder: WIRED_OR_DEFERRED_WITH_REASON — the visual-smoke open/edit/save round-trip exercises the native editor's existing runtime events; if the native surface already emits editor/save events, cite them, else record DEFERRED-with-reason (no new event kinds are added by a removal closeout).

internal_diagnostics: WIRED — the CI guard, build/test matrix, and sweep surface typed failures; a dependency-failure banner appearing for the removed editor during the smoke is a typed diagnostic caught by the visual check.
Palmistry: NOT_APPLICABLE-with-reason — this MT verifies an existing native runtime posture rather than introducing one.
risk_if_missed: Without the closeout sweep + CI guard, a future PR silently re-imports @tiptap and resurrects the removed editor; without the visual smoke, the app could ship with a broken or missing notes surface after removal; without the manual update, users and no-context models are directed to an editor that no longer exists.

risks: RISK-1: The build/test matrix is green but the app has no working notes surface (native editor not actually wired to the notes-open path), so removal shipped a dead feature — a compile-green regression the visual smoke exists to catch.
RISK-2: The CI guard is added but not actually wired into ci.yml (or is a no-op grep), so reintroduction of the editor still passes CI.
RISK-3: The sweep misses a dynamic import or a string-built module path, leaving a runtime-only reference that never fails the build.
RISK-4: The manual is left stale (still references the TS editor), so users/no-context models are misdirected after removal.
RISK-5: The visual smoke edits or 'fixes' native product code to make the screenshot pass, scope-creeping into WP-012 territory instead of reporting a native defect.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Argus visual smoke is mandatory and includes a live open/edit/save round-trip through the native editor; a compile-green matrix without the smoke is not acceptance.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): A negative test reintroduces a forbidden import and proves CI fails; a proof target greps ci.yml for the guard step.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): The sweep covers dynamic import() and string module paths, and the guard asserts the removed dirs/files are physically absent, not just un-imported.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): HBR-MAN same-change manual update ships in this MT with a self-consistency check (no manual page references the removed editor) and a version bump.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Native rich_editor/code_editor source is in forbidden_paths for edits; a native defect found during smoke is reported as a WP-012 finding, not patched here.

research_provenance.source: Grounding audit 2026-07-21/22 of wtc-native-editors-v1: CI at .github/workflows/ci.yml (+ sandbox-cross-platform-gating-check.yml); built-in model manual at app/MODEL_MANUAL.md; user-manual content seeded in src/backend/handshake_core/src/user_manual/ (seed.rs, spec_seed.rs, fixtures.rs, projection.rs) and surfaced by app/src/components/UserManualPanel.tsx + the native src/frontend/handshake_native/src/manual_content_editors.rs. Removed-module inventory from MT-262; removed deps (@tiptap/* x9, yjs) from MT-263; monaco-editor + native-consumed knowledge/loom routes confirmed as KEEP. Build/test commands from app/package.json scripts (build, test, lint, depcruise, test:visual) and the Rust crates (handshake-native, handshake_core, src-tauri). Screenshot-capture precedent: app/scripts/handshake-screenshot-capture.mjs. Field practice: a CI 'do-not-reintroduce' guard is the standard durable control after removing a large surface.
corrections: The closeout proof is operator-visible + Argus, not just green builds: a compile-green removal can still ship a dead notes surface, so the native open/edit/save round-trip is the acceptance evidence.

Manual updates ship in this MT (HBR-MAN same-change), covering BOTH the built-in model manual (app/MODEL_MANUAL.md) and the backend-seeded user manual, because this is the change that makes the native editor the sole notes surface.
The visual smoke is read-only over native product code; native defects are WP-012 findings, keeping this removal MT from scope-creeping into native editor implementation.
